messages:
omar: Follow-up from the RFC thread: we hit a bad loop in practice where a tenant gets revoked, their lease drops, and clients immediately request another lease from a different scheduler shard. Result: eviction storm + repeated revokes. Need a practical handoff.
jen: Yikes. Is the new lease being granted because revocation isn't globally visible? :grimacing:
omar: Exactly. Revokes write to central KV but schedulers read lazily. By the time another shard issues a lease the revoke hasn't propagated.
lee: Two surface fixes I sketched: 1) global revocation tombstone with short TTL consulted by admission, or 2) per-client revocation nonce that prevents new fast-path leases unless the nonce rotates. Both have tradeoffs.
maria: Tombstone is simpler operationally (no client changes) but adds a read on admission. Nonce requires client handshake + we can't trust abusive clients to respect it.
jen: Could we avoid a read on the normal fast-path by layering: consult a local in-memory revocation cache first, and only on miss do an async KV read to populate cache? So most traffic avoids KV.
lee: Yeah, local LRU cache is the plan. Also think we should have a short soft-quarantine window on other shards after a revoke is issued: when a revocation writes, it can also publish a lightweight fanout notification to other nodes to prime cache.
omar: Notification ping helps, but we need to tolerate missed pings. So design = tombstone KV (short TTL) + local cache + best-effort push. Admission flow idea:
```
1) fast local token check -> grant
2) consult local revocation cache (LRU) -> if present, deny/soft-quarantine
3) if cache miss, schedule async read of tombstone KV and meanwhile throttle to probation path (slower fallback, reduced tokens)
```
This keeps admission non-blocking and avoids adding KV latency to the normal happy path.
maria: Important: TTL tuning. If TTL too long we hurt legit customers; too short and we still have thrash. Propose default tombstone TTL = 30s, with a configurable range per-tenant severity.
jen: For false positives we need a rollback flow. Operations can retract a tombstone early, but that is dangerous. Instead, add an appeals channel: verified tenants can request expedited re-eval; automated appeals put tenant into probation (reduced throughput) until validation completes.
lee: Implementation notes: tombstone key format `revoke:{tenant}:{seq}`. Admission keeps per-tenant highest seen `revoke_seq` in cache to detect newer revokes without full KV scan. Tombstone value = revoke_seq + metadata (reason short code). Keep values tiny.
omar: Metrics to add before rollout: tombstone read QPS, cache hit ratio, new-lease-after-revoke rate, probation admissions per minute, appeal frequencies.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: Canary scheduled - revocation-cache shim + probation fallback rolling to 25% edge for 2h at 02:00 UTC.
maria: Ops playbook: how to retract tombstone (manual re-eval), how to force-evict a tenant if we see thrash, dashboards to monitor new-leases-per-revoke.
jen: Action items: I'll capture TTL proposals (15s/30s/60s) + probation rate (20% of previous throughput) in a short micro-RFC. Lee: can you prototype the cache + async KV fetch shim? Maria: draft ops playbook and appeal flows.
lee: I'll also add a stress test simulating a revoked tenant trying to get leases from 50 schedulers to measure false-negative window.
omar: Roll slow. First canary should only enable tombstone checks in probation mode (no hard-deny) so we can measure without mass-impact.
maria: Agree. Ops on-call assigned for canary window.
jen: Posting micro-RFC shortly. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
